A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

nominal income targetry can provide an optimal policy for a wide range of parameters, but that it does so only if it is interpreted as a target for the level of nominal expenditure, not a growth rate.
nominal income targets are not necessarily preferable to money supply targets but they do provide a more satisfactory response to demand shocks.
nominal income targetry is a superior monetary policy rule to a fixed money growth rule.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nominal income targetry may be a useful intermediate step in the transition from a fixed money supply to a fixed price level, and that the optimal policy in the short run is to target nominal income.
, under rational expectations, a nominal income target may be preferable to a money supply target, but only if the price elasticity of demand is less than unity.
nominal income targetry is not necessarily a panacea.
